data.name: SafeNotElevated
data.value: Not running as administrator. Raw disk access requires administrator rights.

data.name: SafeSameDisk
data.value: The source and target are the same disk. You can’t clone a disk onto itself.

data.name: SafeTargetIsSystemFmt
data.value: Target [{0}] {1} is the system disk holding the currently running Windows. Overwriting it will stop this PC from booting.

data.name: SafeTargetIsBootFmt
data.value: Target [{0}] {1} holds this PC’s boot files.

data.name: SafeTargetHasPageFileFmt
data.value: Target [{0}] {1} has a page file that is currently in use.

data.name: SafeTargetReadOnly
data.value: The target disk is read-only. You’ll need to clear its write protection first.

data.name: SafeTargetSmallerLayoutFitsFmt
data.value: The target is smaller than the source, but all of the source’s partitions still fit. (Source {0} / Target {1}) The empty space after the last partition, {2}, won’t be cloned. Partition positions and contents stay the same, and nothing is written to the source.

data.name: SafeTooSmallDetailShrinkFmt
data.value: The source’s partitions extend to {0}, so they don’t fit on the target. To make them smaller, shrink the volumes on the source first.

data.name: SafeTooSmallDetailSectors
data.value: A full sector-by-sector clone is only possible when the target is at least as large as the source.

data.name: SafeTargetTooSmallFmt
data.value: The target is {0} smaller than the source. (Source {1} / Target {2}) {3}

data.name: SafeSectorSizeMismatchFmt
data.value: The logical sector sizes differ (source {0} bytes / target {1} bytes). A sector-by-sector clone between them won’t boot.

data.name: SafeTargetHasDataFmt
data.value: Everything on target [{0}] {1} will be erased. It currently has {2} partition(s): {3}

data.name: SafeSourceLiveSystem
data.value: The source is the currently running system disk, but a VSS snapshot isn’t available. Cloning without a snapshot copies files while they keep changing, so the clone’s parts come from different moments — it’s inconsistent and usually won’t boot. Turn the snapshot on in an environment where VSS works, or boot from other media (such as WinPE) and clone this disk while it isn’t running.

data.name: SafeTargetLargerFmt
data.value: The target is {0} larger than the source. The extra space is left unallocated. After cloning, you can extend the last partition in Disk Management.

data.name: SafeSourceOverUsb
data.value: The source is connected over USB, which limits speed.

data.name: SafeTargetOverUsb
data.value: The target is connected over USB, which limits speed. Take care not to disconnect it during the operation.

data.name: SafeSourceBiosOnly
data.value: The source uses MBR with an active partition (BIOS style) and has no EFI system partition. The copy will only boot on hardware that supports legacy (CSM) boot — it won’t boot from an NVMe M.2 slot or on UEFI-only PCs (NVMe has no legacy boot option ROM). To move it there, convert the copy to GPT/UEFI with mbr2gpt after cloning.

data.name: SafeSourceHibernated
data.value: The source has a hibernation image (hiberfil.sys) — Windows was shut down with Fast Startup. The copy will try to restore the saved kernel state on different hardware and hang on a black screen with no error message. After cloning, “Repair boot” on the results screen turns off resume and clears the image.

data.name: SafeAssertTargetGoneFmt
data.value: The target disk you confirmed, [{0}] {1}, no longer exists. Aborting the operation.

data.name: SafeAssertTargetChangedFmt
data.value: The disk at device number {0} has changed since you confirmed it. At confirmation: {1} ({2}); now: {3} ({4}). To avoid erasing the wrong disk, the operation is aborted.

data.name: SafeAssertTargetReclassifiedFmt
data.value: Target [{0}] {1} has been reclassified as a system/boot disk. Aborting the operation.

data.value: The BCD’s device reference doesn’t point to this disk ({0}) — risk of 0xc000000e at boot. If the source and target are connected together, their signatures collide and Windows re-signs the target. Use “Repair boot” to repoint device/osdevice to this disk’s partitions.

data.name: BcDetailNoControlSet

data.name: BcDetailHwNarrow
data.value: Not all of the standard AHCI/NVMe drivers are boot-start — if moving to different hardware, --universal-restore is recommended.

data.name: BcDetailBiosBootCode
